invariants: A warm cream ARM or BAR swung across the path of a moving thing, at rest in the closed position, never a door and never a wall
The thing it stops is CAUGHT MID-MOTION and intact: paused, never damaged, never broken, never falling

The open book's SPINE is the axle: it passes through the post and continues rightward as the bar itself, one unbroken horizontal shaft, with the pages fanning up from it. No separate disc, no hinge hardware. The bar can only pivot because the book is there
No padlock, no chain, no keyhole, no barrier, no red. Refusal here means the work did not meet the standard, never that someone lacks permission
The way past is visibly OPEN behind the bar, so the gate reads as a decision point and not a dead end
Warm editorial register: cream ground, single-weight wobbly amber ink outline, flat fills only
Absolutely no text, letters, numbers, or readable marks

prose.voice: The moment a standard stops something. Chapter 7's whole claim made visible: a gate is a definition of good made enforceable, so the bar and the book are one object.
prose.lore: Composes with `the-constitution`, which is the standard at rest. Where the constitution is the small warm book of principles a helper checks itself against, the refusing gate is that same book doing its job: the bar it holds shut. Render them together whenever the scene is about the standard ACTING rather than the standard existing.
prose.rules: Always closed and always calm. The stopped thing is intact and paused, because this gate protects work rather than punishing it. Never a padlock: a padlock says you lack permission, and this says the work did not meet the standard. The path beyond stays visibly open, because a gate that only ever refuses is a wall. The joint is the load-bearing detail and it is specific: the spine IS the axle, continuous with the bar. A book mounted beside or on top of a separate pivot disc is a DEFECT, because it says here is a standard and separately here is a gate, which is two objects and a weaker claim.
